nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a type with a zero and a one, and let $f$ be an antimultiplicative arithmetical function with values in $R$. Then $f(p) = 0$ for every prime $p$.
nodes.title: Antimultiplicative functions vanish at primes

If $f$ is multiplicative, then $F$ is multiplicative, and if $f$ is antimultiplicative, then $F$ is antimultiplicative. nodes.title: Real powers preserve multiplicativity and antimultiplicativity

nodes.summary: Let $L$ denote the Rearick logarithm and $*$ the Dirichlet convolution. nodes.title: Rearick's real power and its vector space laws

nodes.summary: Let $U$ be the group of units of the ring of real arithmetical functions under Dirichlet convolution. The units $f$ with $f(1) = 1$, the multiplicative units and the antimultiplicative units form subgroups $U_1$, $U_M$ and $U_A$ of $U$, respectively. Moreover $U_M \le U_1$, $U_A \le U_1$ and $U_M \cap U_A = \{\delta\}$, where $\delta$ is the Dirichlet identity.
nodes.title: Multiplicative and antimultiplicative units form subgroups

nodes.summary: Every real arithmetical function $f$ with $f(1) = 1$ can be written in exactly one way as a Dirichlet convolution $f = g * h$ of a multiplicative real arithmetical function $g$ and an antimultiplicative real arithmetical function $h$.
nodes.title: Unique splitting into multiplicative and antimultiplicative parts

nodes.summary: For every semiring $R$, the identity $\delta$ of Dirichlet convolution on arithmetical functions with values in $R$, given by $\delta(1) = 1$ and $\delta(n) = 0$ for $n \ne 1$, is antimultiplicative.
nodes.title: The Dirichlet identity is antimultiplicative

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a type with a zero and a one. An arithmetical function $f$ with values in $R$ is antimultiplicative if $f(1) = 1$ and $f(p^k) = 0$ for every prime $p$ and every integer $k \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Antimultiplicative arithmetical functions
